This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. These petitions are filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.42/2021 of Mahila Police Station, Hubballi.

entities.text: Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.42/2021
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. While Crl.P.No.100152/2022 is filed by accused Nos.2 to 5, Crl.P.No.100671/2022 is filed by accused No.1.
During the pendency of the proceedings, accused No.2 has died.
3. While accused No.1 is the husband, accused No.2 is the mother-in-law, accused No.3 is the sister-in-law and accused Nos.4 and 5 are the distant relatives of accused Nos.1 to 3.

4. For the sake of convenience, the petitioners are referred to as accused Nos.1 to 5.
5.
Accused Nos.1 to 5 are seeking quashing of criminal proceedings initiated against them based on the complaint filed by respondent No.2.
6. The accused Nos.1 to 5 have contended that the initiation of criminal proceedings against them is an abuse of process of law and it is initiated with a dishonest intention to harass them.

As evident from the complaint averments, complainant is residing in her parents house and the circumstances and situation in which the accused are placed itself goes to show that the complaint is filed by respondent No.2 with an intention to harass them.
Accused No.3 is residing along with her husband in Germany.
She had come to India for delivery.
In view of the health conditions of her parents, she was taken care of by her maternal aunt i.e., accused No.4 who is residing separately at Gurunath Nagar, Hubballi.
The father and husband of accused No.2 died during Covid period and while accused No.2 was taking treatment for Covid and was admitted to the hospital.
When her condition was critical, respondent No.2 left the matrimonial home and chosen to file a complaint.
7. Though there is no prima facie material to connect the accused persons with the alleged crime, the concerned police without making any inquiry have mechanically registered the case.
Accused No.2 is bedridden and not in a position to move about.
Accused No.3 is presently residing along with her husband at Germany.
All the petitioners have been roped in as a measure of arm twisting and prays to allow the petitions and quash the criminal proceedings.
8. Respondent No.1 is represented by the learned High Court Government Pleader.
9. Respondent No.2 has appeared through counsel.
10. Reiterating the complaint averments, learned counsel representing respondent No.2 submitted that the marriage of accused No.1 and complainant was performed on 13.02.2020.
At the time of marriage, the accused No.1 and her family members demanded and received dowry in the form of gold ornaments, cash in a sum of Rs.2 lakhs and household articles.

One week after the marriage,

4 accused Nos.1 to 3 started harassing and ill-treating her saying that she do not know how to work and cook and they used to assault her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 11.03.2020 while she was at the school, her parents came to her house.
However accused Nos.1 to 3 picked up quarrel with them, abused in filthy language and complained against her.
On that day she was sent to her parental home.
11. Again on 10.04.2020, her parents advised her and sent her to the matrimonial home.
The father-in-law of respondent No.2-complainant had a soft corner towards her.
Accused No.1 used to come in a drunken state and abuse her.
Accused Nos.1 and 2 were also assaulting her.
At the time of delivery of accused No.2, respondent No.2 was stopped from going to work.
At that time she was forced to do the household work.
On 22.08.2020 and 14.11.2020, accused No.4 joined accused Nos.1 to 3 in demanding gold ornaments and silver articles.
On 08.12.2020 the father-in- law of complainant died after which, the harassment increased.
During the said period, accused No.2 was admitted to hospital on account of Covid.
The other accused i.e., accused Nos.2 to 4 abused her and directed her to go to the hospital and die there.
12. On 16.12.2020 accused No.1 assaulted her with electric coil and demanded dowry of Rs.1 lakh.
On 10.08.2021 at 11.30 p.m. accused No.1 assaulted her with water bottle.
In this regard on 17.08.2021 she went to the hospital and got MLC report.
On 23.08.2021 she has filed the complaint.
Based on the complaint, case is registered and after completing investigation charge sheet is filed.

Charge sheet makes out a prima facie case and prays to dismiss the petitions.
13.
Heard the arguments and perused the records.
14. As noted earlier, during the pendency of the petition, accused No.2 who was the mother-in-law of respondent No.2 had died.
When the complaint was filed she was bedridden on account of Covid.
She was also admitted to the hospital.
Accused No.3 is the sister-in-law of complainant.
As evident from the complaint averments itself, she is residing with her husband in Germany and at the relevant point of time, she had come to India for her delivery.
Accused No.4 is the maternal aunt of accused No.1.
She is working as a Principal.

Accused No.5 appears to be a distant relative of accused Nos.1 to 3.
15.

From the complaint averments it is evident that right from the beginning of the married life,
there is dis- cordiality between accused No.1 and respondent No.2- complainant.
The complaint refers to serious of complaints and also allegations that accused No.1 used to drink and assault her.
Despite making severe incidents throughout, respondent No.2 has not chosen to file the complaint.
Only after the incident dated 10.08.2021, she has chosen to file a complaint on 23.08.2021 after a delay of nearly 13 days.

Perusal of the complaint averments and the charge sheet reveal that there are no specific allegations against accused Nos.2 to 5.
16.
The main grievance of respondent No.2 is against her husband i.e., accused No.1.
There is also allegations that at the time of marriage, a sum of Rs.2 lakh was credited to the account of accused No.1.

In the absence of specific allegations against accused Nos.2 to 5, this Court is of the considered opinion that continuation of criminal proceedings against them would amount to abuse of the process of the Court.

However having regard to the specific allegations against accused No.1, the Smt. Vishalakshi W/O. Kumaresha Konnur vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152777872/
5 petition filed by him is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Crl.P.No.100671/2022 filed by accused No.1 is rejected.
Crl.P.No.100152/2022 is allowed.

The criminal proceedings initiated against accused Nos.2 to 5 in Crime No.42/2021 of Mahila Police Station, Hubballi for the offence offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are hereby quashed.

SD/-
